mainEntity.name: Can I make my acrylic dentures last longer than ten years?

acceptedAnswer.text: With excellent care, some patients do keep their acrylic dentures for longer than ten years. However, even well-maintained dentures are affected by the gradual resorption of the underlying jawbone, which changes the fit over time. Beyond a certain point, continuing to wear ill-fitting dentures may cause more harm than good to the gum tissues. Most dental professionals recommend regular reviews to assess whether relining or replacement would be more appropriate than continuing with an older set. The goal is always to ensure your dentures are comfortable, functional, and safe.

mainEntity.name: How do I know if my dentures need relining rather than replacing?

acceptedAnswer.text: This is something a dentist can assess during a clinical examination. Generally, relining may be suitable if the denture base and acrylic teeth are still in good structural condition but the fit has changed due to bone resorption. If the acrylic teeth are significantly worn, the base is cracked, or the overall structure is compromised, replacement may be the more appropriate recommendation. There is no single answer that applies to everyone — treatment suitability depends on individual clinical assessment.

mainEntity.name: Is it safe to repair broken acrylic dentures at home?

acceptedAnswer.text: Home denture repair kits are commercially available, but most dental professionals advise against using them as a long-term solution. Poorly repaired dentures may not fit correctly and could cause injury to the gum tissues or alter the bite in a way that places stress on the jaw joint. If your dentures break or fracture, contacting your dental practice for a professional repair is the safer course of action. Many dental practices can carry out same-day or next-day repairs depending on the nature of the damage.

mainEntity.name: Why do my dentures feel loose even though they are relatively new?

acceptedAnswer.text: Dentures can feel looser than expected for several reasons. In the early weeks of wearing new dentures, the muscles of the cheeks, lips, and tongue take time to adapt. However, if looseness persists or develops some time after the dentures initially felt comfortable, it may reflect changes in the gum tissue or underlying bone — a process that can sometimes occur more rapidly than anticipated. In some cases, the gum tissue may have swollen or changed following tooth extraction. A dental review would help identify the cause and determine whether relining or adjustment is appropriate.

mainEntity.name: Should I wear my acrylic dentures at night?

acceptedAnswer.text: Many dental professionals recommend removing dentures at night to allow the gum tissues to rest and recover from the pressure of wearing them during the day. Wearing dentures continuously without a break can contribute to accelerated gum tissue change and may increase the risk of oral infections such as denture stomatitis — a condition caused by Candida (a type of fungus) beneath the denture. Your dentist may offer individual guidance based on your specific circumstances.
